## Research question

> **Which data science skills are most valued?**

"Valued" isn't directly observable, so we measure it two ways:

| Proxy | Definition | What it captures |
|---|---|---|
| **Demand** | Share of data-related postings whose description mentions the skill | How often employers ask for it |
| **Pay** | Difference in advertised salary between postings that do and do not mention the skill, before and after adjusting for job category | What employers are willing to pay for it |


## Data and approach

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
::: {.small}
**Kaggle: *Job Postings with Salaries*** (minmaxer)

- Jobs posted in one week on 4,000+ company career sites, with pay ranges
- Snapshot: **October 5–12, 2026**
- Pairs the skills employers ask for with the pay they offer

**Alternatives considered:** CV/resume datasets (what people offer, not what employers want), course descriptions (what schools teach), BLS data (job types, no skills)
:::
:::

::: {.column width="45%"}
[9,173]{.big-number}<br>cleaned job postings

[226]{.big-number}<br>data science postings, 30 tracked skills

[178]{.big-number}<br>with a usable USD salary
:::
::::

# Value Proxy 1: Demand

## Category "Personalities"

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="58%"}


![](Figures/slides-top5-by-category-1.png)


:::

::: {.column width="42%"}
::: {.small}
**Postings that mention top skills**

| Skill | Postings | Share |
|:---|---:|---:|
| Python | 163 | 72.1% |
| SQL | 133 | 58.8% |
| Machine Learning | 74 | 32.7% |
| LLM | 60 | 26.5% |
| Statistics | 55 | 24.3% |

::: {.small}
- **Python and SQL** are the only skills common (≥ 40%) in nearly every category
- **AI/ML:** Does not feature SQL heavily
- **Analytics & BI:** SQL + a BI tool (Tableau, Power BI)
- **Data Engineering:** SQL, Python, pipelines, dbt, Snowflake, cloud
:::

:::
:::

# Value Proxy 2: Pay

## Data science and the market

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](Figures/slides-salary-histogram-1.png)

:::{.small}

| Group | Postings | Median | Mean | IQR outliers |
|:---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Data Science | 178 | \$165,000 | \$166,885 | 2 (1.1%) |
| Other jobs | 7,412 | \$108,875 | \$120,410 | 78 (1.1%) |

:::
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
:::{.small}
![](Figures/slides-pay-context-1.png){fig-align="center" width="90%"}

::: {style="padding-left: 2em;"}

  - Data Science and AI/ML pay the most
  - Data Analytics and BI pay least
  - Skills common in AI/ML roles will *look* like they carry a premium even when the role, not the skill, drives pay
  
:::
:::
:::
::::






## Salary premiums by skill {.smaller}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="60%"}
![](Figures/slides-premium-plot-1.png)


:::

::: {.column width="40%"}
::: {.big}
- **ML, LLM, PyTorch:** about **+\$28K to +\$38K**
- **Excel, Power BI, Tableau, Data Viz:** **\$50K–\$68K less**
- **SQL:** −\$40K, only because AI/ML (highest paid) rarely lists SQL

**Association, not causation.** Most confidence intervals include zero (n = 178).

:::
:::
::::

# Which Skills Are Most Valued?

## Composite value score

Average of demand rank and salary rank; lower is better.

| Skill | % Postings | Demand Rank | Salary Rank | Value Score | Median Salary |
|:---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| LLM | 26.5 | 4 | 4 | **4.0** | \$190,900 |
| Machine Learning | 32.7 | 3 | 6 | **4.5** | \$182,200 |
| Data Pipelines | 23.9 | 6 | 7 | **6.5** | \$182,025 |
| Python | 72.1 | 1 | 16 | **8.5** | \$165,000 |
| PyTorch | 11.9 | 16 | 2 | **9.0** | \$195,050 |
| AWS | 20.8 | 8 | 12 | **10.0** | \$169,250 |
| Statistics | 24.3 | 5 | 17 | **11.0** | \$164,900 |
| Generative AI | 9.7 | 21 | 1 | **11.0** | \$196,500 |
| SQL | 58.8 | 2 | 22 | **12.0** | \$152,500 |

::: notes
A skill scores best when it is both frequently requested and linked to higher pay. Common-but-cheap and rare-but-expensive skills both get penalized.
:::

## Key takeaways

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
1. **Python is the clearest answer.** It is in 72% of postings and appears across every category.
2. **SQL is still essential.** It is in nearly 60% of postings and present in every job type.
3. **AI/ML skills are where the money is.** Generative AI, PyTorch, Deep Learning and LLMs are linked to the highest-paying roles.
4. **Skills travel in bundles.** Python + SQL + Machine Learning is the core stack.
5. **Role type matters as much as skills.** Data Science and AI/ML pay roughly \$75K more than Analytics/BI.
:::

## Limitations and future work

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Limitations**

::: {.small}
- One-week snapshot (Oct 5–12, 2026)
- Postings from specific applicant-tracking systems; US- and tech-heavy
- Small sample: 226 postings, 178 with salary
- Advertised, not realized, pay; USD only
- Keyword matching can't tell required from preferred
- No seniority adjustment; associations aren't causal
- No supply-side (CV) comparison
:::
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
**Future work**

::: {.small}
- Longitudinal tracking with weekly Kaggle updates
- Geographic pay and company comparisons
- Experience-level analysis
- Salary patterns of skill combinations
- Other job-posting and CV datasets
- Models controlling for location, seniority and industry
:::
:::
::::

## Demand differs by job category

![](Figures/slides-demand-category-1.png){fig-align="center" height="560"}

::: notes
AI/ML: Python, ML, LLMs, PyTorch; SQL in only 7% of AI/ML postings. Data Analytics and BI: SQL plus a BI tool (Tableau, Power BI). Data Engineering: SQL and Python with pipelines, dbt, ETL, Snowflake, Databricks and cloud. Python and SQL are the only skills common (≥ 40%) in nearly every category. Small categories (n < 15) are noisy.
:::

## There is no single "most valued" skill

| Tier | Skills | What the data shows |
|:---|:---|:---|
| **Tier 1 — Must Have** | Python, SQL | Asked for in 60–72% of all postings; appear across every job category |
| **Tier 2 — High Value** | Machine Learning, LLMs, Statistics | Tied to the highest-paying roles; growing demand |
| **Tier 3 — Specialist Premium** | PyTorch, Deep Learning, Generative AI | Less common but linked to the largest salary premiums |
| **Tier 4 — Category-Specific** | Spark, Databricks, dbt, Snowflake | Important in Data Engineering; less relevant in analytics roles |
